stage_transitions.friction_pattern: Top-of-funnel cold decay: qualified accounts sit uncontacted or unresponsive for ~33 days before dying. No won accounts move through this transition, making it a pure attrition gate.
stage_transitions.evidence: 139 lost, 0 won accounts at this transition. Median 32.9 days to loss. 'Cold' is the #1 closed-lost reason at 114 instances, directly mapping to accounts that never convert from Qualified to a booked Discovery Call.
stage_transitions.play: Within 48h of Qualified Account creation, send a personalised NRM-region ACCU price projection (current spot × eligible hectares estimate) with a direct calendar link. Re-ping at day 7 with a 25-year revenue range. Hard-disqualify or recycle at day 21.

stage_transitions.friction_pattern: No data exists for this transition — zero won and zero lost records. The stage either collapses into Discovery Call in practice or is systematically skipped, making it a pipeline visibility blind spot.
stage_transitions.evidence: n_won=0, n_lost=0, both median_days=0. This transition produces no measurable signal, suggesting Discovery Call and Strategy Call may be logged as a single event or the Strategy Call stage is not consistently used by the team.
stage_transitions.play: Audit CRM stage-entry rules this week: confirm whether Strategy Call is being logged as a discrete stage or merged with Discovery Call. If merged, split and backfill from call transcripts so future cohort analysis can isolate this conversion rate.

stage_transitions.friction_pattern: Post-Strategy Call decision paralysis: lost accounts take 12x longer to exit this stage than won accounts. Landholders who don't commit within ~3 days after the Strategy Call rarely convert — they drift into the 'Not for at least 6 months' or 'Insufficient commitment' buckets.
stage_transitions.evidence: Won: median 3 days, n=34. Lost: median 37 days, n=56. A 12x day-gap with n=34/56 gives moderate-to-high volume. '25 years too long' (9 losses) and 'Not for at least 6 months' (45 losses) suggest commitment hesitancy surfaces immediately after Strategy Call.
stage_transitions.play: Send a same-day post-Strategy-Call email with a one-page 25-year ACCU projection anchored to the landholder's specific NRM region and soil type discussed on call. Include a 72-hour SLA initiation deadline tied to next available baseline sampling slot to create legitimate urgency.

stage_transitions.friction_pattern: Mapping stage administrative drag: lost accounts take ~48% longer in SLA/KCT Mapping than won accounts. Likely driven by landholder delays in returning signed SLAs, unresolved eligibility questions, or baseline cost sticker shock stalling completion.
stage_transitions.evidence: Won: median 41 days, n=23. Lost: median 60.8 days, n=29. 'Baseline costs too high' (5 losses) and 'Ineligible (method)' (10 losses) surface here. A 20-day gap with n=23/29 — moderate confidence signal.
stage_transitions.play: At day 14 of SLA/KCT Mapping with no returned SLA, trigger a call to address baseline cost objections directly — offer a cost-benefit breakdown showing baseline cost recouped against projected 25/75 ACCU revenue at year 3. Escalate method-eligibility blockers to AgriProve technical team within 48h of identification.

stage_transitions.friction_pattern: KCT abandonment after issuance: won accounts close in 17 days; lost accounts take 139 days — an 8x gap — before dying. Issued KCTs that aren't executed within ~3 weeks almost certainly reflect landholders who received the document but had no urgency to sign.
stage_transitions.evidence: Won: median 17.1 days, n=23. Lost: median 139 days, n=14. 8.1x day-gap. Despite small lost n=14, the magnitude is extreme. 'Cold' and 'Insufficient commitment' as dominant closed-lost reasons align with landholders holding unsigned KCTs for months before going silent.
stage_transitions.play: Implement a KCT expiry policy: KCTs auto-expire 30 days after issuance. At day 10 post-KCT, call the landholder to confirm receipt and surface any signing blockers. At day 25, send a written notice that the KCT and baseline sampling slot will be reallocated — reissue requires a new queue position.

top_systemic_friction: Top-of-funnel cold decay dominates: 114 of the largest loss-reason bucket ('Cold') maps to 139 accounts lost at Qualified Account → Discovery Call, representing the single largest volume of pipeline destruction. Fixing 48h outreach cadence and hard-disqualification rules at this stage outweighs any mid-funnel optimisation.
era_lift_observation: Legacy era accounts (268) dwarf all other eras combined and likely carry inflated 'Cold' and 'Insufficient commitment' losses from older, less-structured qualification criteria. KCT Process era (44) represents the most structurally clean cohort — use its win/loss patterns as the benchmark for re-qualifying Legacy-era dormant accounts.
